briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Anthropic Claude 5 push reasoning frontiers as US tightens export controls on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AGI race intensifies with multiple frontier labs releasing enhanced reasoning models this month. Geopolitical tensions rise as export restrictions bite into Chinese AI development. Safety concerns mount around production deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with 40% gains on agentic tasks. Anthropic's Claude 5 introduces native multi-agent orchestration. Google DeepMind Gemini 3 and Meta's Llama 4.5 compete on open weights while xAI ships Grok-3.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target multi-agent risks.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp hits 2M units quarterly. Microsoft and Google announce $50B combined data center expansions in Texas and Arizona. TSMC 2nm yields improve for next-gen AI chips.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI emerge from a closed lab or an open-source coalition by 2028?
